finding.claim: Unauthenticated OS command injection in GET /ping: req.query.host is concatenated into a shell command passed to exec(), allowing arbitrary command execution as the server user.
finding.source: req.query.host (tools.js:7), reachable via GET /ping with no auth, server listening on port 3001 (tools.js:28)

trace.note: /ping route registered with no auth guard
raw query value concatenated into shell command string and passed to exec
command stdout returned to client, so injected command output is visible to attacker

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware in file; no allowlist or format validation on host; uses exec (shell) rather than execFile with argv array; no escaping. Array/object query values still yield an injectable string after concatenation. /version (tools.js:16) uses execFile with constant args and /uptime (tools.js:25) runs a constant command, so neither is injectable.

verdict.reason: tools.js:6 registers GET /ping with no auth middleware, and tools.js:7 concatenates the raw req.query.host into a string passed to exec(), which runs through /bin/sh, so an anonymous attacker can inject shell metacharacters; tools.js:11 returns the command output to the client, and no validation, allowlist, or escaping exists anywhere in the file.
